reason: PARTLY REFUTED. The headline update holds, but two of the three supporting claims and the proposed caveat text do not. WHAT HOLDS: probe 48 (56623105, exp79a = exp70g + CI, 0.956 -> 0.957, UP 33) is the only CI submission ever made (poll.log), so no CI variant was selected on the LB. It is deterministic and topology-identical, so on the public embryo the CI delta is certainly >= 0, with a true size somewhere in (~0, 0.002). The refiner never saw that embryo, just as it never saw the private ones. So it is a real out-of-embryo read (n = 1 embryo), and 'unknown-to-slightly-negative' should move up. R22-RC-A's line 'probe 48 is not a private transfer record' was too strict. WHAT FAILS. (1) The 'MEASURED 4/4 clips in both embryos' evidence is IN-SAMPLE. The refiner was trained on 44b6 + 6bba, which are exactly those clips (scan_recheck.notes l.6; CONTEXT l.2984 'in-sample for the refiner'). The raw in-sample refiner RMS is 1.06-1.30 um against a base of 1.51-1.84 um, so the gain from averaging is inflated by the fit and says nothing about transfer. (2) 'No fitted offset (z bias unchanged)' is false on 6bba_784a78c9. Bias (dz,dy,dx) goes (0.751,0.314,0.499) -> (0.612,0.210,0.328) um, and |bias|^2 goes 0.91 -> 0.53 um^2, so about 40% of that clip's MSE cut is a learned 6bba offset (refiner_raw bias 0.30/0.09/0.17). Only the 44b6 clips are a pure variance cut. (3) RMS is not the metric. On the same 4 clips the J change is -0.0029/+0.0125/0/+0.0029, so it is not 4/4. The alpha curve is jagged too (a0.35 -0.0015, a0.5 +0.0022, a1 -0.005), and R25-RC-B found the same. A caveat reading 'lab lower error 4/4 clips both embryos' would therefore mislead the user at the finals pick. With only the public read and the Mamarin prior (~3 in 4 for public-best gains) left, P(private CI >= 0) is ~0.6-0.7 and the central value ~+0.0003-0.0005. That is the finding's range, shaded down, and still one embryo. FEASIBILITY: it is a wording change with no code. Coverage is fail-soft and topology identical (dummies 121,252 nodes / 81 forks). But (a) 'answer the user's pending question: CI morning files yes' oversteps. The question is the USER's to answer (CONTEXT 10:19Z: until the user says yes, morning files are non-CI), so the session may only recommend. (b) A single 09:30Z (12:30 MSK) cutoff is safe only for exp79a-weight files: L_hi 9.45 h -> reads ~18:57Z, before the 20:00Z tick. The CI stacks run longer in the dummy: exp87a 1,870 s and exp83c 2,055 s vs 1,712 s. Scaled naively, that is ~10.3 h and ~11.3 h hidden (logged band 9.4-10.9 h), which would need submission by ~09:25Z and ~08:25Z, and exp83c would sit near the 12 h cap. (c) Keeping exp75 (#37 + CI) as the private hedge is consistent. CI on cap 4 is untested on the LB, but CI does not touch topology, so it should roughly add.
fix: Keep the verdict change, but correct the text. Finals-card CI caveat: 'CI: one out-of-embryo public read, exp79a vs exp70g 0.956 -> 0.957 (UP 33; true delta in (0, 0.002)); topology byte-identical, fail-soft coverage; lab = 4 clips IN-SAMPLE for the refiner (RMS lower 4/4, but J -0.0029/+0.0125/0/+0.0029, sign flips with alpha; part of the 6bba gain is a learned offset); private P(CI >= 0) ~0.6-0.7, central ~+0.0004; one embryo.' To the user (MSK first): RECOMMEND, do not decide, that CI morning files be allowed. Cutoffs: exp79a-weight CI files (exp75, exp79a-family) by 12:30 MSK (09:30Z); heavier CI stacks (exp87a K+CI) by ~12:00 MSK (09:00Z); SEC+CI (exp83c) by ~11:15 MSK (08:15Z) or not at all in the morning. Non-CI by 14:30 MSK (11:30Z). Keep exp75 as the private-hedge candidate with the rule exp75 >= 0.955 -> pair {best public, exp75}. Curator: I-028/CI card gets the corrected caveat, not the finding's '4/4 both embryos / no fitted offset' wording.
realistic_gain: Decision-quality only; no score change by itself. If it tips a finals pick toward a CI file: expected private ~+0.0003-0.0005 vs its non-CI twin, P(>= 0) ~0.6-0.7, downside ~-0.001 if the refiner does not transfer to the private embryos.
